# What a scene changes

Each section is one guide topic. The Studio's "How to write this" and the wizard's `readGuide` show the same text.

<a id="guidance"></a>

## Narrator guidance

Topic `guidance`.

Field: `checkpoints[].guidance`: text, or `{ "all": text, "members": { <roster id or name>: text } }` (`schema.ts` `MemberGuidance`, `engine/checkpointGuidance.ts`).

- **What it does.** Private direction for how the beat plays. Plain text and `all` reach every reply generation in the beat. A member's entry is staged only while that member is drafted to speak, never at rest. Quiet and impersonate runs get no guidance at all, and no pacing hint or check outcome either.
- **Good.** `"Two days of road. Let {{story_role_companion_a}} and {{story_role_companion_b}} take initiative beside {{story_player_name}}."` Three to six sentences of pressure and intent. Secrets in the member's own entry: `"members": { "oren": "The keepers paid you to bring strangers in…" }`.
- **Bad.** `"At dawn the water drains and reveals the drowned king."` (an ending, which a reply can paraphrase as a spoiler); a secret in shared guidance; calling the player "the player" (characters then call them "the player" too).
- **If wrong.** A member key no cast member has reaches nobody (`guidance-member-unknown`). Openings and guidance that end on "What do you do?" teach the narrator to end every reply on a question.

<a id="author-note"></a>

## Author's note

Topic `author-note`.

Field: `effects.author_note`: text, `null`, or `{ text, role, position, depth, interval }`, with `inject_blackboard: true` to append the story's state memo (`runtime/effectsApplier.ts` `authorNoteText`, `applyAuthorNote`).

- **What it does.** Written into SillyTavern's Author's Note when the beat starts, so it steers every reply in the beat. `role` is `system`, `user` or `assistant`; `position` is `before`, `after` or `chat`; `depth` and `interval` are SillyTavern's own. `null` clears the note.
- **Good.** Sun-ruins: `{ "text": "[Keep the pacing relaxed. Describe the guild tavern's noise …]", "position": "chat", "depth": 4, "interval": 3, "role": "system" }`. A story can set `"author_note": null` on the start beat only, to clear a stale note, and steer through objectives and guidance instead.
- **Bad.** A note on one beat and none on the next, when the old note no longer fits.
- **If wrong.** A beat without its own note keeps the previous beat's (`checkpoint-inherits-author-note`: "The model keeps being told an earlier checkpoint's note here."). While a beat has its own note the objective line is not injected (`engine/agency.ts` `objectiveLineApplies`), so prefer objectives and guidance to checkpoint notes.

<a id="world-info"></a>

## Beat lore

Topic `world-info`.

Field: `effects.world_info`: `{ "enable": [{ "lorebook": "<book>", "comments": ["<entry title>", …], "until"?: "chapter" | "<checkpoint id>", "lasting"?: true }], "disable": [ … ] }` (`engine/worldInfoEffects.ts` `readWorldInfoEffect`, `loreAlongPath`).

- **What it does.** Switches lorebook entries on and off along the story's path. Every entry any beat names belongs to the story (its gated set). The set rests off, and on every apply (a new beat, a reopened chat, a rollback, a story swap) it is rebuilt by replaying the chat's path from the start, so a reopened chat ends in the same state as a continuous one. With per-chat gating (the default) that rebuild happens on each scan's own copy of the entries, never in the lorebook file. Entries outside the set are never touched. Only beats carry beat lore; transitions do not. An intermediate the story expands into a generated stretch is never entered itself, so its own `effects.world_info` is played by the stretch's first generated beat (the same switch, replayed with the path): to turn a passed scene off for the downtime that follows it, put the `disable` on that intermediate.
- **Every enable has an end.** In a story with chapters, an entry a beat switches on ends when the path leaves that beat's chapter (the default, `"until": "chapter"`). `"until": "<checkpoint id>"` ends it when the path enters that checkpoint instead, chapters or not; `"lasting": true` keeps it on until a beat switches it off. The end is part of the path replay, so a reopened chat, a swipe or a rollback agree; a later beat that enables the entry again starts a new end. In a story without chapters an entry without `until` lasts until a beat switches it off. The Studio's Effects editor shows the end beside each enable. Switch: Settings › World & lore › "Lore ends with its chapter" (Author view, on); off, nothing ends on its own.
- **Lore budget.** One prompt should carry no more than about 2,500 tokens of the story's own lore. The Studio adds up, along every path from the start, the constant entries switched on plus the largest keyword entries lore-select may force (its `top_k`, else 8) and warns at the beat where it passes that (`lore-path-over-budget`: "Lore switched on along this path is larger than the lore budget, so it crowds older chat history out of the prompt in a long chat."). Give scene, cast and truth entries an end rather than keeping them on for the whole story: the scene's chapter, or `until` the beat where they stop mattering; mark `lasting` only what every later beat needs.
- **Good.** `{ "disable": [{ "lorebook": "Sunken Ruins Checkpoints", "comments": ["CP ruined-gate - Scene"] }], "enable": [{ "lorebook": "Sunken Ruins Checkpoints", "comments": ["CP flooded-hall - Scene"] }] }`, with the book generated from the same source as the story so a title can never name a missing entry. A cast sheet for one act: `{ "lorebook": "Ruins", "comments": ["Cast - Guards"], "until": "cp-gate-open" }`. A truth every chapter needs: `{ "lorebook": "Ruins", "comments": ["Truth - The Pact"], "lasting": true }`.
- **Bad.** A secret in a constant entry with no character filter, which every drafted member reads, so any character may name the traitor before the reveal. The effect only toggles entries; it has no per-member target, so make a secret narrator-only or keyed. Keeping every cast and truth entry on for the whole story with `lasting`: by the last chapter the prompt carries all of it.
- **If wrong.** With per-chat gating (the default) these entries stay off in their files, show as off in SillyTavern's lorebook editor and stay off with the extension disabled (`world-info-rests-off`). An entry named by a misspelt title is simply not found. Require the book under `requirements.lorebooks`. An `until` that names no checkpoint never ends (`world-info-until-unknown`: "This lore never ends where you meant: no checkpoint has that id, so it stays on until a checkpoint switches it off."). Within its chapter, a scene enabled at a beat stays on until a later beat switches it off, through a whole generated stretch too, unless the expanded intermediate disables it.

<a id="preset"></a>

## Preset

Topic `preset`.

Field: `effects.preset`: a preset name, or `{ name, settings }` (`runtime/effectsApplier.ts` `resolvePreset`; `runtime/samplerOverlay.ts`).

- **What it does.** A per-request sampler overlay for this beat's replies. A name is matched exactly against the connection's own presets (never fuzzy); `settings` carries the samplers inline. Only samplers the request already sends are overlaid, only on the player's visible replies, only while the beat is active. The selected preset is never changed.
- **Good.** A slightly hotter sampler for a dream sequence: `{ "name": "Dream", "settings": { "temperature": 1.1 } }`.
- **Bad.** A preset name that exists only on another API, or one that carries no sampler the connection sends.
- **If wrong.** The effect is refused with a reason in the journal, and the beat plays with the normal samplers. Text Completion and Chat Completion connections only.

<a id="background"></a>

## Background

Topic `background`.

Field: `effects.background`: a file name, or `{ name }` (`schema.ts` `BackgroundEffect`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readBackground`).

- **What it does.** Switches SillyTavern's background when the beat starts, and again when the chat is reopened.
- **Good.** `"background": "tavern day.jpg"`, a file the install has (the wizard's `lookupBackgrounds` lists them).
- **Bad.** A background whose picture shows the twist; a name invented for the scene (`pawnshop_interior`) that no file carries.
- **If wrong.** A name the install lacks does not switch anything (diagnostic `background-missing`: "The scene does not change: the install has no background by that name."; checked against the install's list, with or without the file extension, when the Studio knows it).

<a id="stage-transition"></a>

## Stage transition

Topic `stage-transition`.

Field: `effects.transition`: a kind, or `{ kind, ms, color }` (`schema.ts` `TransitionEffect`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readTransition`, `sprites/motion/cues.ts`).

- **What it does.** Sets how the sprite stage changes into this beat when play enters it. `dissolve` (the default when the field is absent) crossfades the background when the beat also switches it; `fade` covers the stage with `color` and uncovers it; `wipe` sweeps the color across and off; `iris` closes a circle to the centre and opens it again; `cut` switches with no transition and no crossfade. `ms` is the whole transition (0 to 5000; defaults dissolve 600, fade 1000, wipe 900, iris 1000), `color` a hex color (default `#000`). Presentation only: it plays on a forward step into the beat, never on reopen, rollback or a chat switch, and writes nothing to the story's state.
- **Good.** `"transition": { "kind": "fade", "ms": 1200 }` on the first beat after a time skip; `"transition": "cut"` for a sudden shock.
- **Bad.** A wipe on every beat; a long fade on a beat the player reaches every few turns.
- **If wrong.** An unknown kind, an `ms` outside 0 to 5000, a color that is not a hex, or an unknown key is a validation error naming the field. The player's stage effects setting (`sprites.effects`) and reduced motion (SillyTavern, the system, or the story's `display.motion: false`) shorten every transition to a short crossfade or skip it.

<a id="backdrop"></a>

## Animated backdrop

Topic `backdrop`.

Fields: `effects.backdrop` on a checkpoint and the story's `backdrop_defaults`, each `{ layers, weather, time, indoor, intensity, loop }` (`engine/backdropSchema.ts`, `validate/backdrop.ts`, `src/backdrop/`).

- **What it does.** Animates the scene behind the chat: the background still (or a video loop of it, when one is ready) with weather and light layers drawn over it. Presentation only: it writes nothing to the story's state and never delays a turn. With nothing authored the backdrop is derived from the story's own state: a `weather` quality (rain, storm, snow, fog, wind, clear), the clock's `time_of_day` / `is_night`, `tension_current`, and whether the background looks like an interior. Derived picks: rain or snow outdoors, a storm adds mist and lightning, wind blows dust sideways, interiors get floating dust (lit areas only) and firelight after dusk, fireflies only on clear nights in green outdoor places (forest, garden, meadow, lake), and a slow camera drift everywhere. Tension darkens the edges and thickens weather a little; it never speeds the weather up. `backdrop_defaults` applies to every beat; a beat's `effects.backdrop` overrides it field by field.
- **Fields.** `layers`: a list of `{ kind, intensity, speed, color, mask }` or plain kinds; `[]` means no layers. Kinds: `rain`, `snow`, `embers`, `dust`, `fireflies`, `fog`, `flicker` (firelight), `drift` (slow camera move), `shimmer` (water or heat haze), `parallax` and `depthFog` (need a depth map of the background). `intensity` 0 to 1, `speed` 0.1 to 4, `color` a hex, `mask` `sky`, `water` or `none` (where `shimmer` shows: `sky` and `water` need the background's scene mask and show nothing without it; `none` is a faint heat haze over the whole picture). `weather` and `time` replace what the state says for this beat; `indoor` true keeps sky weather out; `intensity` 0 to 1 scales every layer. `loop`: `"pre"` asks for a video loop of this beat's background to be made when the story is set up (never shown before the beat is reached), `"auto"` lets one be made when the GPU is idle, `false` keeps the still.
- **Good.** `"backdrop": { "weather": "rain", "layers": ["rain", { "kind": "fog", "intensity": 0.3 }] }` on a storm beat; `"backdrop": { "indoor": true, "layers": ["flicker", "dust"] }` in a candlelit cellar; `"loop": "pre"` on the two or three places the story returns to.
- **Bad.** Heavy rain on every beat; `loop: "pre"` on every checkpoint (each loop costs minutes of GPU); a layer meant to reveal something the player has not found.
- **If wrong.** An unknown kind, weather, time, mask or loop value, a number out of range, a kind listed twice or an unknown key is a validation error naming the field. The player's Display settings (Animated backdrop, its effects, depth, loops and intensity switches) and the system's reduce-motion setting win: it shows the still only (SillyTavern's own Reduced motion option does not).

<a id="scenario"></a>

## Scenario

Topic `scenario`.

Field: `effects.scenario`: text, or `""` / `null` to clear (`schema.ts` `CheckpointEffects`, `validate/checkpoints.ts`, `runtime/storyScenario.ts`).

- **What it does.** Sets the chat's own scenario text (`chat_metadata.scenario`) along the played path: text sets it, `""` or `null` clears it, and a beat without the key keeps what the path before it set. In a group SillyTavern then sends this one text instead of every member card's scenario. It waits with World Info until the story's requirements are met. A `/cp activate` jump plays the target's own value, so a jump target that authors none plays with the chat's scenario from before the story. A scenario the user typed into the chat is never overwritten; restarting or removing the story puts back what the chat held before.
- **Good.** Framing only: genre, places, the arc's name (one per beat works well): `"scenario": "The Sunken Ruins in the dry season. The village of Lowmarsh is the party's base."`
- **Bad.** A `scenario` with the final foe or a secret in it: every member's prompt carries it.
- **If wrong.** A story that sets none leaves every member card's scenario in the prompt at once; the author view names those cards ("N character card scenario(s) frame this chat and the story sets none").

<a id="cast-changes"></a>

## Cast changes

Topic `cast-changes`.

Field: `effects.cast_changes`: `{ "enable": [card names], "disable": [card names] }` (`runtime/effectsApplier.ts` `applyCastChanges`).

- **What it does.** Mutes and unmutes group members when the beat starts. Only enabled members respond. It changes the group itself, which outlives the chat, and it is restored when the chat leaves the story.
- **Good.** The start beat disables everyone who enters later; each later beat enables the characters who enter there: sun-ruins `cp1` disables `Ponticius` and `Luke`, `cp2` enables `Ponticius`.
- **Bad.** Disabling a companion the player has just recruited, because the beat's list was written before play.
- **If wrong.** The authored list always wins over what happened at the table: a companion the party took along is dropped by the next beat's disable. If play can recruit someone, gate the cast change on a quality play sets. Put every enabled character the player may address into the beat's speakers. A name with no card on the install switches nothing (diagnostic `cast-member-no-card`: "This character never joins the scene: there is no card by that name, so it cannot be switched on and the story never reads as ready."; it also covers `requirements.members`). A cast change may name a cast member by card name or by roster id (the id resolves to the member's name); an entry that is neither changes nobody (diagnostic `cast-change-unknown-member`: "This cast change switches nobody on or off: the name matches no cast member, so whoever it meant stays as they are."). Everyone a checkpoint switches off needs a checkpoint that switches them on again, or they stay muted through their own scenes (diagnostic `cast-member-never-enabled`: "This character stays muted for the rest of the story: a checkpoint switches them off and no checkpoint switches them back on."). The wizard's agent cannot finish while a cast member has no card or the cast it created has no group.

<a id="npc-replies"></a>

## NPC replies

Topic `npc-replies`.

Field: `effects.npc_replies[]`: `{ trigger, member, kind, text, instruction, ask_player, maxTriggers, probability, after_member, new_chat_only, enabled, id, once_per, cooldown_player_turns }` (`schema.ts` `NpcReplyEffect`, `validate/checkpoints.ts`, `validate/talkPacing.ts` `readReplyScope`, `runtime/effectsApplier.ts` `fireNpcReplies`, `runtime/npcReplyRewind.ts` `npcReplyMayFire`).

- **What it does.** Lines a character speaks on their own. `trigger` is `onEnter` (the beat starts), `afterSpeak` (after a character reply; `after_member` narrows it to one speaker) or `sceneBreak`. On `onEnter`, `after_member` fires the line only when the chat's last line is that member's, so a hook can follow the narrator's entering line. `kind: "scripted"` posts `text` verbatim; `kind: "llm"` has the member generate, and its `instruction` reaches that member alone, as a private direction for that one reply ("Direction for X only, this reply: …"), cleared when the reply ends (on any trigger). `ask_player: true` (llm only) adds "turn to {{user}} and ask them exactly one short question in your own voice, then stop" to that direction; for that one reply it wins over the pacing notes' "no closing question" wording, but never lets the member ask what the player does or narrate the player. When the reply still asks more than one question, only its last question is kept: earlier question sentences leave the visible reply (a quote or action left holding only a dropped question goes with it, a short follow-up such as "Last night?" joins its question with a dash), the rest of the line and the thinking stay as written, and a reply the trim would break is kept whole. It runs once per generated reply, swipes included, before the story reads it; the switch is Settings › Characters › Speaker direction › "Keep one question when a character asks you" (on by default). An `ask_player` line is skipped while its member is switched off in the group. Entering lines fire in declaration order, each waiting for the one before to finish. `maxTriggers` caps how often one reply fires in its `once_per` scope (default 1): `story` (the default) counts the whole chat, so a revisit does not re-arm it; `entry` counts each visit to the beat, so the line can return when the story comes back; `player_turn` counts since the player's last message. `cooldown_player_turns` is how many player messages must pass between two fires of the same reply (default 2 for `afterSpeak` and `sceneBreak`, 0 for `onEnter`); extra party replies no longer shorten it, because it counts the player's turns, not messages. `id` names a reply for its counters (letters, digits, `_ . : -`); without one the reply is counted as `trigger:member:index`, so give a reply an `id` before reordering a beat's replies, or the moved ones count afresh. Two replies with one id in a beat are a load error. `probability` is a seeded chance, `enabled: false` parks a reply without deleting it. `afterSpeak` and `sceneBreak` lines share the beat's speech budget with the speaker chain (see Pacing profiles and speech budget): a line the budget has no room for is held, and the journal says so; entering lines (`onEnter`, the opener and the hook) are the entry sequence and do not draw on it. Fired counts persist, so reopening never repeats a reply; a swipe, edit or delete of the posted line re-arms it. An `afterSpeak` reply never answers a line the story itself posted (an opener, a hook or another NPC reply), it waits while the last reply asks the player something (the same reading as `yield_on_question`, and off where the beat sets that `false`), and a generated (`llm`) reply starts only through the same guarded starter as a chain voice: it waits (up to 10 seconds) while a reply is being written or a speaker chain still holds the floor, never starts while the player is typing, and gives way when the player sends first; a reply that could not start is not counted, so it can fire on a later turn. A later beat's entering lines wait for the player's answer when the reply before them asks the player something; if that reply is then edited, swiped or deleted, the wait is checked again at the next reply instead of holding on to text that is gone, and deleting earlier messages moves the wait with them.
- **Lines written for someone else.** A character's reply sometimes goes on to a line headed with another character's name or the player's (`Bram: "…"`, `**Bram:**`). Right after the reply arrives, before the story reads it, the reply is cut at the first such line; the thinking is never changed, and a reply the cut would leave nearly empty (under about 40 characters) is kept as written and noted in the log. Prose such as `"Fine," Bram said.` is not cut. Switch: Settings › Characters › Speaker direction › "Cut lines written for someone else" (on).
- **Names and the repetition penalty.** With DRY on in your preset (Text Completion), the cast's names, given names, aliases and your persona name are added to that request's own DRY sequence breakers, so names the story repeats are not bent into misspellings. Your preset is not changed. Switch: "Protect names from the repetition penalty" (on).
- **Good.** `{ "trigger": "afterSpeak", "member": "Oren", "after_member": "Mara", "kind": "llm", "probability": 0.6, "maxTriggers": 2, "instruction": "Oren answers what the guide just said. He does not decide for the party." }`.
- **Bad.** A scripted line with a time or place in it ("As dusk falls…") on a trigger that can fire anywhere.
- **Chapter hooks.** Any beat can open with a party member turning to the player: list the narrator's entering line first, then `{ "trigger": "onEnter", "member": "Mara", "kind": "llm", "ask_player": true, "after_member": "Ruins Narrator", "instruction": "…" }`.
- **If wrong.** A dusk line can fire at dawn, "Oren turns up in the library" can fire at the gate, and a tavern line can fire after the party has left. Word scripted lines to fit wherever they fire, or use `llm`. A scripted greeting on top of an entering reply introduces the character twice; prefer an `llm` opener there. Give `afterSpeak` a probability and `sceneBreak` a `maxTriggers`. An instruction that writes what the player does, or asks what the player does, gets the warning `npc-reply-directs-player`: "The character is told to write what the player does or to ask what the player does, so the reply may decide for the player or read like a game master's prompt." `ask_player` on a scripted reply is a load error. `once_per: "player_turn"` on an entering line counts nothing, because an entering line fires when the beat is entered: the info diagnostic `npc-reply-scope-unused` says "An entering line fires when the beat is entered, never per player message, so this scope never counts anything."

<a id="experimental-effects"></a>

## Experimental effects

Topic `experimental-effects`.

Fields: story `reasoning` and checkpoint `effects.reasoning` (`off`, `low`, `medium`, `high`; `schema.ts` `CHECKPOINT_REASONING`), checkpoint `complications` and `complication_after` (`runtime/spikes/sp6Complications.ts`), story `clocks` (`runtime/spikes/checkClocks.ts`).

- **What it does.** Reply thinking resolves checkpoint `effects.reasoning` first, then story `reasoning`, then the install's Reply thinking setting. Studio → Story → Reply thinking edits the story default. The override switch is on by default. It only budgets a llama.cpp setup that already thinks; it never opens a thought. `low` allows 128 thought tokens and can break group reply form; Studio warns when speaker direction is authored. `complications` are lines released into a beat that has stalled, behind their own default-on spike switch: after `complication_after` (default 3) player turns in a row whose every reply read below the tension target, the next unused line rides the next reply once. A turn with several replies still counts once. `clocks` (spike `checkClocks`, default on) are danger clocks: each `{id, size (default 4), ticks_on: [{check, on: miss|weak, ticks}], near: {at, line}, full_line, checkpoints}` ticks once per check per visit on a matching outcome; from `near.at` filled the near line rides each reply late in the prompt until the clock is full, then `full_line` does. Fill is read from the story's own boundary log, so a rollback undoes ticks exactly; it never gates a transition. Lines must be safe for the player to see.
- **Good.** A story that plays the same with both switches off; a spike only adds to it.
- **Bad.** A story that only works when a spike is on.
- **If wrong.** Where the switch is off nothing happens, so a story that depends on these does not play as written.
